data.title: Oracle Stock (ORCL) Erases Earlier Gains and Falls After Earnings
data.description:
The post-earnings bounce in Oracle's (ORCL) stock was short-lived. In early afternoon trading on Sept. 11, ORCL stock had given up an earlier 6% gain and turned negative as investors and analysts consider the company's latest financial results. In afternoon trading, Oracle's shares were down 1% with downside pressure appearing to build on the stock heading into the weekend.

ORCL stock appeared to be headed for a nice gain on the day after the technology giant reported better-than-expected financial results and raised its guidance. The company posted earnings per share (EPS) of $1.92, which beat the $1.74 consensus expectation of Wall Street. Revenue totaled $19.35 billion, which topped the $19.14 billion that had been forecast on Wall Street. Sales were up 30% from a year earlier.

Oracle's Deteriorating Finances

Unfortunately, the strong print does not appear to have been enough to overcome other challenges that Oracle is experiencing, namely with its finances. Oracle, which is mostly known for its software products, is pivoting to artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. However, Oracle is in a weaker cash position and has a lower credit rating than the hyperscalers it is competing against in the data center space.

As a result, Oracle has $125 billion of debt and negative free cash flow of $5.4 billion. The company said in its latest earnings report that its capital expenditures rose to $28.50 billion from $8.50 billion a year earlier. These figures have likely given investors pause with ORCL stock. The deteriorating finances have pressured Oracle's share price. ORCL stock has declined 48% over the last 12 months.

data.title: HP Stock (HPQ) Soars Despite RBC Capital's Hold Rating — Here's Why
data.description:
Shares in PC maker HP Inc. (HPQ) jumped by 7% to around $35 per share on Friday afternoon. This came despite a new Hold rating from RBC Capital's five-star analyst David Paige. The rally followed bullish comments on product demand for PC rival Dell Technologies (DELL). DELL stock jumped by 11% to $563.

Why RBC Capital Is Cautious of HP

On August 26, HP released its fiscal Q3 2026 earnings. The PC maker's revenue came in at a record $15.7 billion, up by 12.5% from last year.

Its earnings per share also rose by roughly 11% to $0.83, aided by a $0.11 boost from government tariff refunds. However, the California-based company flagged profit pressure on its Personal Systems segment, its biggest business division.

data.title: Chewy Stock (CHWY) Falls 5% on Downgrade from JPMorgan Chase
data.description:
Shares of pet product retailer Chewy (CHWY) are down 5% after the stock received a downgrade and price target cut from JPMorgan Chase (JPM). Analysts Margaret Hoffman and Doug Anmuth downgraded CHWY stock to a Hold-equivalent neutral rating from a Buy-equivalent overweight rating previously. They also and cut their price target on the shares to $24 from $29.

The new price target is 14% higher than where the stock currently trades. In a note to clients, the analysts cited continued macroeconomic pressures and muted organic growth as reasons for the downgrade to Chewy stock. The lowered rating and price target cut come after Chewy recently reported disappointing financial results.

data.title: Vicor Stock (VICR) Soars 11% on New Manufacturing Site Acquisitions
data.description:
Vicor (VICR) stock was up 11.13% on Friday after the modular power components and systems maker announced new acquisitions in a press release. The company said it is buying a 334,000-square-foot building on 66 acres in Merrimack, New Hampshire.

It is also buying 54 acres in nearby Hooksett. The two sites will support Vicor's ChiP Fab-2 and Fab-3. Together, the fabs are set to have nearly one million square feet of space. The move comes as use of ChiP Fab-1 in Andover, Massachusetts, nears its current limit.

ChiP Fab-1 has been built out to 320,000 square feet on 16 acres. The new sites will let Vicor add much more capacity as demand for AI hardware grows. The company said ChiP Fab-2 could be ready for its first use within about one year. The added space is meant to give OEMs and large cloud companies more room to scale their AI systems.

The company also said that its tech can deliver the power needed by advanced AI systems. It also sees the new fabs as a way to give customers a U.S. source for key power parts. According to the company, this expansion will add to its ability to serve the AI hardware market from more than one ChiP fab. data.title: Dow Jones Today: DJIA Climbs on CPI Report as Consumer Sentiment Sours
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is up 1.14% on Friday following an inflation update from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS). The Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% in August, matching estimates but accelerating from 0.1% in July. On a year-over-year basis, CPI increased 3.4%, in line with expectations and unchanged from the prior month. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% from July and 2.4% year-over-year. Economists had expected gains of 0.2% and 2.5%, respectively.

Surging gas prices accounted for more than one-third of August's increase, with the gasoline index climbing 3.9% during the month. Prices have continued to climb this month, with the national average sitting at $4.29 per gallon. Wireless phone service prices also jumped 5.9%, marking the largest increase on record.

Rate hike expectations rallied following the report. The probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 16 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting rose to 86.7% from 72.4% a day earlier, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

data.title: CPI Card Group Stock (PMTS) Falls 15% on a $50M Secondary Offering
data.description:
CPI Card Group (PMTS) stock was down 15.37% on Friday after the financial payment card services company announced details of an offering in a press release. The company said certain stockholders tied to Parallel49 Equity have priced a secondary offering of 2,337,323 shares at $21.50 per share. The deal is set to bring in about $50.3 million in gross proceeds before fees. The offering is expected to close on or about September 14, subject to the usual closing terms.

CPI Card Group is not selling shares in the deal and will not get any of the proceeds. The selling stockholders are also giving the underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 350,598 more shares. Any extra shares would be sold at the same $21.50 price, less the underwriting discount.

The deal gives the selling stockholders a way to sell part of their stake in CPI Card Group through a public market deal. The company said the sale is a registered underwritten secondary offering. As a result, the transaction does not add cash to CPI Card Group's balance sheet or raise new shares for the company.

data.title: Starbucks Stock (NASDAQ:SBUX) Notches Up After Calling for a Safer Seattle
data.description:
Coffee giant Starbucks (SBUX) and the city of Seattle have been at odds since Katie Wilson took office as mayor, and now, Starbucks is joining a coalition of major Seattle businesses calling on Seattle to be a safer place. Investors were reasonably pleased about this stance—unsafe cities generally do not call people to their coffee shops—and Starbucks saw a fractional boost in its share price in Friday morning's trading. Starbucks stock has seen a 21.15% rally in its share price over the past year.

Seattle, Safen Up!

Starbucks joined a coalition of 38 business leaders including the Seattle Mariners, among others, to call on the City Council, along with Mayor Katie Wilson, to delivery a "100-day public safety action plan." This included such moves as putting surveillance cameras back in areas where criminal events happen frequently, and establishing clear goals for police response times, ensuring that police are where they need to be when they need to be there.

The letter from the coalition noted that voters expected Seattle to "…act with urgency, fund the actions needed to improve safety, and provide a clear plan for measuring progress." Considering that only 34% of respondents in a recent public opinion poll believe that the city has a solid plan for public safety, it is not surprising that Starbucks would come out in favor of improvements in this field. Starbucks wants a safer city, because so much of its plans depend on people willing to sit in cities for a long period of time drinking coffee.

data.title: Micron vs. Sandisk: The Opportunity Tilts in Favor of One AI Memory Stock, Says Investor
data.description:
Micron (NASDAQ:MU) and Sandisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) are two names that have drawn a massive amount of investor attention over the past year. Both have benefited from the surge in AI-related memory demand, but they offer investors different exposure to the market. Micron is benefiting from tight DRAM supply and strong demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), while Sandisk is more exposed to NAND and the outlook for flash memory.

That makes the comparison more interesting than simply looking at which company is producing the strongest results today. Both are trying to make their businesses less vulnerable to the sharp boom-and-bust cycles that have historically defined the memory industry. Long-term customer contracts are playing an important role in that effort, but the underlying supply outlook for DRAM and NAND could ultimately matter just as much.

Looking at both companies' prospects, an investor using the pseudonym Delta Analyst (DA) believes Sandisk has made more progress on the contractual side. Its New Business Model agreements cover around half of FY2027 bits and two-thirds of FY2028 bits. The agreements generally run for more than four years and include pricing mechanisms designed to provide protection if NAND prices weaken.

Micron has taken a similar approach with its Strategic Customer Agreements, although coverage is currently lower. The agreements cover around 20% of DRAM volume and one-third of NAND volume, with many contracts extending through 2030. They include take-or-pay commitments as well as price floors and ceilings.

So Sandisk has the more extensive contractual protection. But contracts don't tell the whole story.

The bigger question is what happens to supply. DRAM is expected to remain tight through 2027 as HBM takes up a growing share of manufacturing capacity. HBM requires more wafer capacity to produce comparatively fewer bits, essentially putting pressure on the amount of capacity available for conventional DRAM.

NAND faces a different outlook. Manufacturing improvements, process migrations and additional capacity could result in looser supply conditions during the second half of 2027. That creates a potentially important difference between the two companies.

There are, however, some factors that could ease the tight DRAM supply outlook. Samsung, SK hynix and Micron could redirect more wafer capacity toward conventional DRAM if it becomes more profitable than HBM. China's CXMT is another potential threat. The company is expanding DRAM production and has begun producing HBM3E in small quantities.

The investor does not regard CXMT as an immediate equivalent to the established HBM players, but its progress could become more significant from 2028 onward. If CXMT expands conventional DRAM capacity while successfully scaling HBM3E, it could put pressure on the industry's current supply discipline.

Sandisk also has an advantage when it comes to cash generation. Its recent free cash flow represented around 56% of revenue, compared with roughly 44% for Micron. Micron is also heading into a period of much heavier capital spending as it expands manufacturing capacity.

DA therefore sees two different strengths. Sandisk has built a stronger contractual defence against the next memory downturn, while Micron has greater exposure to the part of the market where supply is expected to remain tight for longer.

After weighing those factors, Delta Analyst rates Micron a Buy and Sandisk a Hold, preferring the former over the next 12 to 18 months. The investor believes the combination of DRAM tightness, strong HBM demand, growing contractual revenue and substantial earnings power gives Micron the better opportunity. (To watch Delta Analyst's track record, click here)

That preference is not without caveats, however. DA is deliberately assuming that today's exceptional margins will fall as supply responds. CXMT's expansion, changes in wafer allocation and the eventual normalization of memory supply could all weaken Micron's advantage. Sandisk could also surprise on the upside if its contracts prove capable of protecting margins even after NAND conditions loosen.

For now, though, the investor sees Micron as offering the better combination of memory-market exposure, earnings durability and potential upside.

Wall Street's stock experts see no reason to choose between the pair, with the analyst consensus rating both stocks as Strong Buys. Micron is expected to gain 60% over the next year, given the average price target clocks in at $1,563.93. Sandisk's average target stands at $2,145, pointing to 12-month returns of 31%.
